utterances.text: Yes. In an unofficial way, without a document. I'm not insisting that it was by telephone. Perhaps it was in a conversation or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. I understand that. You -- yesterday I think you considered the possibility that you received that news on the 11th from Minister Alispahic, and I just wanted to ask you about that. Given your use of the term "unverified information" there, does that make it more or less likely that Mr. Alispahic was the source of that material?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is less likely. Mr. Alispahic, as the Minister of MUP - I don't know if I would have used this term "unverified in some village," if that was to him there are some other key places. I said that it was possible that it is from Alispahic or perhaps from some of his -- or one of his men. I don't know. But it would be risky to state anything definite on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, I suppose -- could I ask you this: If Bakir Alispahic had personally told you this information, the likelihood is that you would have used a different phrase than "unverified information." Is that an accurate statement?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Right now I cannot really imagine that situation. In any case, it would have been more reliable than had it come from somebody else, in view of his function.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, again, I won't read the document out to you or read it into the transcript, but effectively in this letter you assigned appropriate tasks to Nermin Eminovic based on the limited information that you had at the time. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I offer that document for tender, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I'm moving through a number of documents of this nature one by one. And I'll try to do them in chronological order as much as possible, but let -- let it be clear that if you notice that these documents are being put in an unchronological order, you feel very free to point that out, bearing in mind your knowledge of the way these documents are labeled as well. Very well. Now, the next question I have is that you -- you ultimately received that Dzankovic report with the -- with the Salihamidzic attachment which has already been shown to you, but I think your evidence was that that document was quite delayed in reaching you and didn't in fact get there until the 20th or so of September. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, there are some other documents that seem to arise between that time, and now I'm going to take you to those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please now be shown -- its 65 ter number is D165, and its DD number is DD00.0770, and it will be MFI225.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just excuse me a moment, Mr. Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor and -- and members of the Court, I just indicate so that it's clear what's happening here, that I'm going to take him through a number of documents in a chronological way to indicate what effectively occurred during the course of the -- before, during and after the Uzdol matters and also concerning the Grabovica matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. So is that document before you on the screen now a document which appears to be dated 15 September 1993 and appears to be signed by you? And I'll ask you whether it is you in fact who signed it in a minute. But do you have that document in front of you there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Can I just confirm that that is your signature on it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this document is -- is headed by a comment regarding -- or using the terms "participation of Bosnian -- or Republic of Bosnian and Herzegovinian members in the events of Grabovica village, report requested by," and then it's got an address. Would you just explain what the function -- do you see underneath the top -- the top left has got the -- the originating address, "Sarajevo, on the 15th of September," and underneath that is the words -- on the left-hand side: "Participation of ARBiH, Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina members." Can you just explain the structure of this document for me very briefly. What's the function of that passage there on the left-hand side of the page?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was drafted -- this is the first time I'm seeing it though, although it's my document. There's my signature on it. It was drafted in response to a report I received from the security chief of the 6th Corps, as a response to the document that we were looking at previously. Your Honours, here you can note one thing: We were simply looking for Dzankovic. You could see that the security administration didn't know what the situation was in the field and that problem, who is in charge and which of the security organs in the control and command aspect are there, who would be able to take on their part of the responsibility from the military security aspect. So we were sending out papers to Mr. Eminovic in the 6th Corps and then to Mr. Dzankovic via the 6th Corps because we practically didn't know where he was. I don't know if we received a response from Mr. Eminovic, but if we have it, then you will see that it was not something that was satisfactory to me. He was just providing a picture of the situation that could not satisfy me, because it was talking about the corps security chief, and there's a vast difference. I'm digressing here, but there's a vast difference between that institution and Dzankovic. That person had a service of 15, 16 people, military police battalion, commander, and so on. So since I received a response like that to my document sent to Mr. Eminovic on the 12th to the 6th Corps, I wasn't satisfied with the response. I'm now continuing what I actually started to explain. We were sending this document to Dzankovic to see what he could do, and he is being issued with these tasks here and to make a report so that he could provide us with something that we could evaluate and know what actually had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I take it at this time, when you sent this letter, you didn't know that Dzankovic had already written his report dated the 13th of September, because that hadn't arrived at your -- at your centre yet.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I tender that document -- sorry, I offer that document for tender as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There are going to be more such documents again. And if it's a document that you don't recall seeing or haven't seen for many years, just feel free to take as long to acquaint yourself with it as you need. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please be shown -- its 65 ter number is D166. Its ERN number is DD00.0772, and it's to be MFI226.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: While that's being brought up on the screen, could I just ask you a question concerning numbers of military police and so on. Were you aware of -- of the military police establishment within the 6th Corps in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure that I understood the question. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. That's okay. Well, look, I've jumped to another topic and it's a bit unfair. Perhaps if you'd just take the time to look at that document first and then we'll -- I'll ask you those questions in a minute. Okay. Now, this -- the document that you're now being shown appears to be a document signed by Eminovic and is dated the 17th of September of 1993, and it seems to be addressed to you personally. Did you -- did you receive this letter from Eminovic at some stage?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The notes in the upper right-hand corner are mine, but this is the first time that I am seeing this paper in 11 years, but the notes are mine for Vahid to inform himself, then also it -- these are my initials, for this to be included in the bulletin. This is already the 17th of September. It's a dynamic, very lively phase of data compilation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that's how we can describe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll gratefully adopt that comment. There are some other documents we're going to show you. Just -- I just want to get some particulars about the document. First of all, the handwritten part that refers to Vahida, is that a reference there to your employee, Vahid Bogunic, who has figured in other notes that have been mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we seem to be -- have some confusion here. Is D166, is that the document we were just shown, which is MFI226?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Is that the one which is on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The D166 is a Defence ERN number, if that's causing confusion -- sorry, 65 ter number. The ERN number you'll find at the very top, in the middle, at the very top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It's different than the one you read out, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if there's an objection, it had better be clarified because I don't want to mislead the witness or the Prosecutor, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the number is DD00.0774 or 0772?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes, it's been pointed out to me. The Bosnian version is 772. That's what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Jasarevic. Okay. So that was my first question. That concerned Mr. Bogunic. Now, the next question was: It should be possible to -- yes, I'm sorry, pardon me. I did have another question from the text. If you -- if you could look towards the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand yours is all one page. There's a section probably 15 lines from the end that refers to a report from Zuka, and you might see -- I'll read you the sentence here: "I would like to emphasise that Zuka was the only one who was able the enter this area without any consequences, that he wrote a report on the event, but we do not know what is written in it, and that he would forward it to the SFK in Sarajevo." Do you have that passage in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had this earlier on. I said that I couldn't remember this report. After all, it was sent to the SFK and not to the security administration, which is quite an important difference, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, certainly. Well, I -- sorry, pardon me. Yes, we acknowledge the difference, and -- and I agree with that. If it was sent to the SVK and the Chief of Staff of the SVK, Sefer Halilovic, was on the terrain -- sorry, if it was sent to the SVK in Sarajevo, as is stated here, and the Chief of Staff of the SVK was on the terrain in Herzegovina, to whom would you expect any such report to go at the SVK?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the nature of things, the commander would receive these. If the commander is absent, in the worst of cases this should -- this should end up in the hands of the operations centre of the Main Staff. In the worst of cases I say, because this report would sort of tend to be a combat report, and that would be outside the purview of the service, and Zuka was no member of the service, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, that was -- that was going to be my next question. In the normal course of events, a combat report from Zuka, such as the one described there, wouldn't go to you; it would go to Commander Delic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would go to Delic. Now who would process this sort of document in an operative way is really not something that I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, okay. What is the significance of the date at the very bottom of the page there? It says -- the stamp on the last page says: "Main Staff of the Armed Forces security administration. Strictly confidential." It gives a number, and then it says: "20th of September." Does that mean that your office received this on the 20th of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness will need to see the next page in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. That's precisely what it means. Here you see the incoming stamp of the administration. You can see it right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plus the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender as well. I'd now ask that the witness be shown -- this is another document, which is not uploaded into the system as yet. It is D573. That's the -- that's the 65 ter number. And copies are now available to be distributed. Yes. Could I just indicate with respect to this, Your Honour, there have been a number of acts of treachery by the Defence against the e-court system in terms of using paper copies. We are going to be provided with a scanner, and we are receiving, I have to say, a great deal of support from the Registry in this regard. We believe physically the scanner now exists and is to be delivered, and we hope to have it in place this evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And we do undertake to do as much as we can to avoid having to use paper copies in the future, and we're sorry that we're doing it here. This document we'd seek to be MFI227.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jasarevic, again, this is -- I don't know whether this is such a document. Have you seen this document in recent times, or is it a -- one from long ago?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the first time I've laid eyes on it. I would even go so far as to say that I could have provided a more detailed statement to the OTP had I seen this paper. I didn't sign this, but you can see my initials right there in the lower left corner. So, on the one hand, I produced this document; and on the other, I didn't sign it. Now, there's something that doesn't tally about this, but it is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I just want to be sure that we're -- I'm not putting to you a document over which there's any suspicion. Does it appear to be a genuine document, as far as you can see?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it has a formal drawback: I didn't sign it. You see my initials on the left-hand side; although, anyone could have placed them there. But the nature of the problem analysed by this document and given who it was sent to, I am convinced of the latter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Well -- thank you. Sorry. Pardon me. Okay. Well, in relation to this, is the -- does the information in it assist your memory to -- to explain to the Court what information you had on that date, on the 16th of September, 1993? Does it accurately reflect what you knew on that day?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is no way I can possibly remember what I knew on that day. Unlike Grabovica, I had precious little information in relation to the Prozor area. We kept looking, which is easy to see if you look at this document. We kept trying to track down information. We insisted that we be informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. There's a number of other documents which -- which I'll put to you in that regard as well. But at this point anyway, are you able to recall or say what was the source of this unverified information that's referred to in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you heard of the -- the killings at Kriz, Uzdol, and other hamlets in that area in whole or in part through Croatian media? In other words, can you recall whether these incidents featured in the Croatian media at or around this time?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that there were references to Uzdol. I can't say I heard this myself. It may have been one of my operations officers, one of my subordinates, but I know that what happened at Uzdol was debated. I remember there was one or possibly more special reports that we wrote and sent to our superiors, the persons that we reported to, and I remember that in that special report we stated that the information being forwarded had been obtained from people who were on the ground. This information spoke about some specific circumstances where civilians had been killed because there was fighting going on, because the clashing parties were very close, not far apart, and because there was artillery fire. I'm not sure if I'm about to use the right term -- random fire. The conclusion that we based on that was that casualties were inflicted on their own forces as well as the enemy; friendly fire, in other words. It was based on information like this that we also included another bit of information that we had; namely, among the civilians who were killed, there were some armed persons who had joined in the fighting with the HVO, as members of the HVO. So this was more or less the gist of the report that we sent along to our superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I should indicate to you, Mr. Jasarevic, we have a number of such reports which I'm going to show you and get you to comment on soon. This one now I'm really putting because I want to preserve the chronology of -- of your involvement, frankly, in the matter and of your service's actions and inquiries that -- that you undertook. Before I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer this document for tender as well, if the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask you, before I move on to another document, could just ask you this: When Croatian media alleged that the Army of Bosnia had committed a war crime or an atrocity, were you inclined to accept that as 100 per cent accurate merely because it was on Croatian television?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not. We always took into account the fact that there was a lot of propaganda included in what the media featured. A security service should certainly not be tempted to take such things as face value. As soon as you have a great deal of propaganda, you can hardly take anything for granted. But we certainly didn't underrate these reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were simply out to get information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And once again, it's -- it's fair to say that you would include in the information that you processed all operative information, including what was on the media? Is that accurate? In other words, you didn't totally disregard it just because it happened to come from Croatian television; you gave it the weight that you thought was appropriate. Is that a fair way to put it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not something that I can be sure about, but it certainly made sense, what you're suggesting. This should have affected our position in some way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And of course you did make the inquiry which is right in front of us here on this page on the 16th of September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well -- and there are some other documents which I'm now going to move to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown another document. This is an exhibit in the case already, and it's, I think, D159.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I believe it to be D, but I don't want to take the Prosecution's credit if that's wrong. But it's the 159th exhibit. It's D.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This document that's going to be shown to you now, Mr. Jasarevic, is not a document of yours. It appears to be an inquiry by Stjepan Siber -- it's okay, I'm just describing what you're going to be looking at in a minute. An inquiry directed to the 6th Corps. And when it comes on the screen, I'll get you to comment on it. All right. Now, do you see that that's a document from Siber to the 6th Corps -- in fact, to the 6th Corps command?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that it comes from -- from Stjepan Siber, who at that time was standing in officially for the -- for the commander of the army, who is --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Standing in, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So bearing in mind that it comes from someone of the high level of Mr. Siber, who do you expect -- or to whom should that document have gone within the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is command communication. This is someone who is standing in for a commander and, therefore, holds a command position. On behalf of the 6th Corps, this should go to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In functional terms, this is a letter from Siber to Gusic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if that's how you understand these names. It doesn't necessarily mean that Gusic was there to receive the document. Maybe it was his deputy. That's in terms of their respective positions. Now, in reality, it depends on their respective whereabouts at the time. I'm not sure if Gusic received this document personally. It's -- it's purely speculative because it depends whether he happened to be at the command at the time or maybe he was away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I understand that. And I'm not asking you to engage in that particular speculation. All right. Well, could I ask you: Although that's not a document that's addressed within the professional line, did it come to your knowledge that the acting commander of the army was inquiring of the 6th Corps exactly what had happened at Uzdol? Did that -- were you aware that that inquiry was being made?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No., I don't recall that. I don't believe I knew at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That document is already in evidence. I now ask that the witness be given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, could we have a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My apologies. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I now ask that the witness be shown another document. This is D -- the Defence 65 ter number is 167, and it's DD00.0776, and it's to be MFI227.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. My apologies. Could that please be 228. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could I just ask you, first of all,

utterances.speaker: MR. JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this a document that you've seen in recent times?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. From the day it was produced in all likelihood. But this is my signature, and these bodies or persons referred to here in the lower left-hand corner are my people, and this is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And I take it this is -- is one of the documents produced at that time which you described as a reasonably hectic time of -- of correspondence concerning events in Herzegovina. Could I ask you this about this document. This is directed to -- this is another of the documents directed to Nermin Eminovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, unlike some of the other documents, it doesn't refer, or at least I don't notice it referring to -- to previous correspondence. What was the trigger for this particular letter? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. There's a reference here to the need to brief the Presidency and the SVK. The use of the term "Presidency," does that -- is that a reference to briefing a session of the Presidency or a meeting of the Presidency, or does it refer to a particular individual?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is a conditional use of the term. That's what Mr. Bogunic wrote. That's what I explained, who was informed. That's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document could only have been received by the president of the Presidency and Mr. Ganic. So much for the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And what is the significance of that last paragraph there: "The report should be forwarded to the security administration by 1200 hours on 19th of September. Because of the obligations towards the Presidency, please ensure that the report is sent by this deadline." Does that mean that there was already in existence a -- a request from the Presidency to you or your organisation, or does it have some other meaning?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am in no position to comment on this, simply because I can't recall this. It was a long time ago. I assume that probably we were not satisfied with the reports we were receiving from people on the ground. That's one possibility. It may be that the president required additional information, but it could have been anything. I really can't remember, and I wouldn't like to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender as well, Your Honours. Could the witness please next be shown another document. This one is 65 ter number D168. Its ERN number is DD00.0778, and it is to be MFI229.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When this document appears on your screen, you'll see, Mr. Jasarevic, that it's a -- a similar document but it uses the word "warning," and I'm going ask you to comment on that -- on that term. Do you have the document in front of you yet?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now,--

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honours. I've been advised that I should slow down what is already in some respects a very slow process, but I shall -- I shall slow down, Your Honours. Could I indicate after consideration in the break, Your Honours, I think it's a noble ambition that I will not be able to fulfil to finish tonight. But as you'll see, we're moving through, and -- and there will be certainly room for another witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, Mr. Jasarevic. Now, with regard to this document here, can you indicate why it was that this was headed as a warning?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the first time that I am seeing this document since it was created, but it's absolutely clear why it's formulated in this way. That's also stated. You can see that it says here "our telegrams number," so and so. The security service was asking for a report from the 6th Corps security service. We have no other way. We cannot order such a report, but we were insisting, requiring, asking to have this information sent to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I notice here on the third line of the first paragraph there - at least that's the English situation - that there's a reference to -- there's a reference to events in Grabovica village, Jablanica municipality, as well as to the villages of Uzdol and Kriz, in the Prozor municipality. In referring to Grabovica, you'll recall that earlier on I -- I showed you a document where you made an inquiry of the 6th Corps concerning Grabovica. Is it that correspondence which is being referred to here, where you refer to Grabovica, or is there some other correspondence that occurred in respect of Grabovica that I haven't provided to you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that we continue here to ask for information in respect of Grabovica, and it has helped me now. It has refreshed my memory regarding crimes at a different location and our attempts to receive information of which we had much less, and the information was different than the one referring to Grabovica. I cannot remember all the details about the cause and effect specifically when I'm commenting on this document, but we, here you can see, are continuing to find -- to ask for information from the service covering the location where the crimes occurred, covering these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And just a final formal question: Is that your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I'm sorry, I always have to ask that question, to be -- to clear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I offer that document for tender. Could the witness please now be shown a -- another document. This is 65 ter number 169. It is ERN number DD00.0780, and it's to be MFI230.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you have that document in a legible form before you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. Now, does this appear to you to be a response to your -- your warning letter and indeed the previous conversation -- the previous correspondence to which you've already attested?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I can't state that decisively, but probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. In any event, are you able to indicate that this was addressed to you personally and came from Nermin Eminovic, arriving at your offices on the 21st of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can I just say this arrived on the 21st of September. You can see that in the lower left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you'd better explain, because I'm -- I'm a strict amateur about these matters. But that -- that stamp at the bottom left indicates the time it was received; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the 29th of September -- 21st of September. That's what it states on the document that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the communications you were having with both Eminovic and Dzankovic, it appears to -- on the document so far -- I'm putting a general question now, not one directly related to this text, but I'll come back to this text in a minute. It appears that with respect to Grabovica you made inquiries both of -- of Dzankovic and also of Eminovic, but with respect to Uzdol you made inquiries of Eminovic alone. Am I right in that, or have I missed something?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain that by the fact that Eminovic is part of the chain of command, an institution which has force, physical force. It has a detachment of 16 people and a military police battalion, so this is a stable function. However, Dzankovic is something else. He's a free shooter, if you permit me to express it like that. He's simply a member of the inspection team. He's not an organ of any command which is commanding and which has all the attributes that go with it and can act in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender as well. The next document I would like the witness to be given the opportunity to look at is -- is 65 ter number D77. Its ERN number is DD00.0295, and its MFI number is 231.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The document that's coming up now appears to have the form of a weekly report, and I'd just ask you to take the -- take a moment to look at it. It's -- it's in a form that you may be able to assist us with and explain. But would you just take a moment to check that document, first of all. It may be that it's on more than one page in the B/C/S. It certainly is in the English version. It has three pages in the English version. And, Mr. Jasarevic, for your convenience, you had better be the one who indicates when you need to turn over the page with that document. When you've looked at that first page you indicate. And then the court staff will help by turning over the page.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please scroll the entire text so that I could look at the whole thing and then we can go back to where you want to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can scroll further. I would also like to see the end of the document at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, you're under no time pressure here. You're entitled to -- to look. I'll just indicate to you to assist that I have a -- the questions I have chiefly relate to the passage that's on -- that's near to the end of the -- of the document and refers to the work of the SVB in working on the investigation of possible crimes committed against civilians in the village of Grabovica in Jablanica municipality and the villages of Uzdol and Kriz in Prozor municipality. You feel free to look at the whole thing as much as you need to, but that's -- that's where I'll be asking you questions.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please look at that part of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I believe it will be the last page of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you see, Mr. Jasarevic, somebody has underlined in the B/C/S version the area of interest. It's just above heading 4, "Proposed measures." And the part of the text that I'm interested by is --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you see there that you've -- you've mentioned that the: "SVB monitored the security situation in the city." And I take it by "the city" you meant Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what part of the text this refers to, but if it's about the city, then I think it refers to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. If -- if -- I mean, you'll -- you will be better at reading this document than I am, so if there's any context that you think you need by reading other parts, just don't hesitate to do that. But the bit that interests me is the underlined part and the bit following that, which is: "They are working on the investigation of possible crimes committed against civilians in the village of Grabovica, in Jablanica municipality, and the villages of Uzdol and Kriz, in Prozor municipality." Now, what I wanted to ask you about: This is -- that was the typical sort of information to record in a weekly report such as the one we have before us; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is part of the operative report when all the administrations submit reports according to combat readiness elements, it's a kind of overview of what the service was doing in the period covered. Then there are different functions that the service is in charge with. Then we have "Zahid" signed at the end of this document. He was the person who was at the head of that section -- or department. "Section" is used here. This was a processing of all the activities that the service performed in a given period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can I just ask you a question -- the passage I just referred you to concerning Grabovica and Uzdol is followed by a sentence which says: "Cooperation with the MUP has continued and so has the exchange of information with the intelligence administration." Now, what -- my question is: Does that sentence relate to the -- to what went immediately before it; namely, the work of the SVB in working on the investigation of possible crimes in Grabovica and Uzdol, or is that cooperation with the MUP about something different?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is probably a general remark which may not necessarily rule out what you said specifically. But I think that this is just a general remark, that this task of cooperation is being implemented. I think this is what is being alluded to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Finally, a formal question: Is that your signature at the end of that document?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I've already said who was the person who actually drafted it, Zahid, which -- he's the one who actually processed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender as well. Now, I move now to -- this is a document which is Defence 65 ter number D21, and its ERN number is DD00.0070, and it's to be MFI232.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you now have in front of you a document described as "Special report" and dated the 20th of September?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a special report. This is the cover page. I have the beginning of the text here, but before that I saw the cover page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the format for these special reports that I mentioned which we sent to our superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. And just again, I have to ask the formal question: Is that your signature at the end of that document?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature. And on the left side is Visca Hamza, who is the author of this document Hamza Visca was the head of the analytical section in the security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This document asserts a number of facts relevant to the -- to what happened at the villages around Uzdol. Are you able to recall what was the source of information that allowed these facts to be put into this document? For example, did this information come from Enver Buza and the Independent Prozor Battalion, or from their professional body, or did it come from the 6th Corps, or did it come from some other source? What are you able to tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the sources or on the basis of which it was written. Definitely it -- something like this is never written just off the top of one's head. There must be documents on -- based on which these reports were created. They were created on the basis of information that we processed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Whilst you can't remember the precise documents there that -- that were relied on in this case, through other witnesses in the case we've seen certain documents that circulated within the 6th Corps, and I wanted to ask you: Would it be the normal practice for a combat report, for example in this case, from the Independent Prozor Battalion, to be assessed personally by you back in Sarajevo, or would that task be performed in the normal course of events by the 6th Corps themselves and they would send you a summary of that? And I indicate I have such a report from the Independent Prozor Battalion that I'll show you unless you tell me that that -- it would never have arrived with you.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command and control principle in the military was to go from down to higher levels. You would go from the battalion, then the brigade, and the corps. You wouldn't bypass the brigade unless it was an independent battalion. This is a principle, and I stand by that. However, if any of the operatives from the service from any level arrived - and this is the institute - arrived at some sort of information by operative means, he could form an official report about that purely to save time, and that document could be treated as a primary document. It would be evaluated -- the source would be evaluated. And then it could be taken into account. But in principle it went from one service to the next upwards along the vertical line from one commander to another, and it would not reach -- and then it would reach the operative centres which analysed this information and then decided on activities that needed to be implemented and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, I understand that. Thank you. At all events, you having made proper and thorough inquiries so far as you were able to do in the circumstances, came to the view that -- to the views expressed in this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. These are the views formed based on certain documents. Again, I must say that -- I've already said something like this yesterday. This kind of document is usually the result of information acquired in the field, and this would be forwarded in order to inform the people who were our superiors. We did not usually check this information ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that, and I -- I mean no criticism by this, but would you look at the last paragraph there, because in this paragraph it appears that you went a step further than simply relaying information. And again, this is no criticism at all, but I just want to clarify what the position is. In that last paragraph, was it the case that you, having made certain inquiries, were prepared to draw the conclusions that are expressed in that final paragraph; namely, that based on the above information, you -- it was obvious that no massacre had taken place at all but, on the contrary, the HVO leaders were circulating a false story?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is a sort of reaction that's kind of freewheeling and it was probably provoked by the media. When we're talking about the media, probably he was prompted to draw such a conclusion, such a liberal conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And the fact is, I suppose, that at that time it was just impossible to send investigators onto the terrain at Uzdol because Uzdol had actually been recaptured by the HVO the very same day of the battle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And even if that were possible, it would not have come from the administration but would have taken the usual order --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- for such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I now ask that the witness be shown another document. This document is DD00.2660, and it's to be MFI233.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This document is -- that's about to be shown to you -- no, you don't have it yet. The document I'm seeking to show you is a document that bears the date 21st of September, 1993 and a signature that may be your signature. Would you mind just looking at that document and seeing -- first of all, is that your signature on the bottom?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again, I should ask you: Is this a document you've seen in recent times, or is it one that is from the old days?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it, and I also saw it recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I saw it recently, but I also remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this document here is a response to the earlier letter that was sent by Namik Dzankovic dated 13th of September but which only arrived at your centre after a delay of about a week; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it arrived on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And am I right in -- in suggesting that this is a response to that letter?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. It was a lapse. It didn't arrive on the 20th. The response to this letter arrived much later, sometime in the first half of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise. No, my question was misleading there. It wasn't your answer; it was my question. What I was -- what I was asking you was: Did Dzankovic's original letter arrive at your -- at your centre on the 20th of September and did you then respond with this letter?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And later on I'm going to show you a letter from Dzankovic which may be an answer to what you've put here, but for now we'll just deal with this one. Now, this letter here was -- in the tasks that you assign or what you -- what you ask him to undertake I take it is an attempt by you to give him some realistic jobs that he could do in the unusual circumstances that he'd told you about. Is that the fact?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, in fact, you -- you went so far as to specifically tell him to be very careful and watch out for his own safety.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because all the documents that we were receiving indicated that the area was dangerous. We'd had indication that everything had been placed under control there by a crime. A man was actually murdered, which was supposed to lead us to conclude that anything was under control. And then there was this document, which was a set of instructions, professional instructions for Mr. Dzankovic to deal with it to the best of his ability. In the title, you can see that these are operative tasks. There was no possibility to -- to carry out an inspection. It was just for him to do the best he could. Based on the document he sent us, as well as the attachment by Mr. Salihamidzic. Together with my legal assistant Mr. Goran Radovic [phoen], whose initials you can see in the lower left-hand corner, I concluded that these instructions or tasks would be the most adequate at the time for Mr. Dzankovic to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you say. And just in relation to that, you had information that a man had been murdered. And let me just clarify what -- what you're referring to there. Were you referring there to the claim made by Ramiz Delalic himself that he had imposed order upon the situation in Grabovica by the means of executing a soldier? Is that the incident to which you refer?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's the incident to which I refer, but not to Ramiz Delalic's report. I think it was in a different report that I saw that. Was it Dzankovic's report or an official note by someone? I believe it was in another document that I saw that. I'm not sure if -- if the timing is the same, but it is true that in each and every document that we received from our people on the ground there were warnings about danger, danger in the area, and they said that only Zuka could go there. You could assume that there would be danger, life-threatening danger, in fact, to Mr. Dzankovic's life as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I should confirm both for your sake and for the record that you're correct; there's -- I'm not suggesting to you that there was actually some sort of written report from Ramiz Delalic in which he admitted this but, rather, that indeed in the -- the Dzankovic/Salihamidzic material there is such a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And yes, I should, I think, ask you one other question about this. You mentioned at point 5 of that document the -- that: "Mr. Dzankovic should undertake to establish the necessary cooperation with Jablanica SJB for realisation of these tasks." Is the SJB -- would you just explain to the Court what is the SJB.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public security station, the one in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's under the Ministry of the Interior. It's one of their own units, and it was a unit at the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I now ask that the witness be shown another document. This is -- now, this is a document that's not in the computer and copy -- copies will have to be provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And could this document -- this is D -- Defence number -- 65 ter number D404, and we ask that it be MFI234.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, what we have here is a document purporting to be a transcript. It's a Prosecution document with an ERN -- or once a Prosecution document with an ERN number, 1 -- 01472382 upon it. And what I'd ask you to do is just -- just read over it, first of all. Because it's only a transcript and we are in no position to assert to you its genuineness or not, what I want to do is give you the opportunity to read it yourself, see whether -- whether you recall that conversation, and whether you're prepared to say that -- whether this is an accurate transcript or not, because it purports to come from you but I want to be clear whether it really comes from you or whether it's from somewhere else. When I say "comes from you," I should rephrase that. It purports to feature you was a participant in the conversation, but it's for you to tell us whether that's correct or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, are there dates for this conversation?.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there aren't dates. And if it's a question of inference. When this document -- if it's accurate, first of all, and in fairness to the witness, he should tell us really whether it is or not. If it is accurate, it may be possible to infer the dates from the subject matter in it. So that's the process. But I think in fairness to the witness he has to be given to chance to go through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As you read, Mr. Jasarevic, I just want to make the -- the comment to you that there's a note on it saying "made late in September," but that note saying "late in September" is a later addition by some other person, and you don't need to be bound by that in any way. That's just -- that might having nothing to do with the case whatsoever. What I ask is that you finish reading that and then you can give a response to what's contained in it on a number of levels. Very well. Mr. Jasarevic, I'm not suggesting to you for a moment that this is your document or that you produced the document, but what do you say about that conversation? Do you recall such a conversation between yourself and Sefer Halilovic one morning such as that has been -- well, in the terms that are before you in that document?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I really can't recall this. I can't see a date or a signature, for that matter. This is purportedly a transcript. Someone probably taped this secretly. I'm not sure who wrote this. It is possible that this conversation actually took place. If I look at the substance of the conversation, especially the last part, talking about the conversation with Dzankovic and his mother, this jogged my memory in relation to certain details that I had already forgotten about his mother's health. I -- I thought it was about her legs, and I can see now the problem was her eyes. But in order to vouch for the authenticity of this document, this is something that I simply cannot do based on -- on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I understand that. And -- and since you say that you can't vouch for the authenticity of the document, then I won't ask you to say anything about it at all. But as to contact with Sefer Halilovic, could I ask you the general question about what actually occurred around that time. Was it -- to your knowledge, did Sefer Halilovic return to Sarajevo approximately -- in or about the 20th of September and stay in Sarajevo for a couple of days after his trip to Herzegovina before he returned back down to Herzegovina again? Does that accord with your memory?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recall one way or other whether he came back from Herzegovina at that time, or is that just too long ago to say?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't recall. I'd be glad to be able to recall, but it was just such a long time ago. I may have seen him; I may not have seen him. We may have been in touch; we may not have been in touch. I just can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In any event, you would not dispute this, would you: That -- that Halilovic did call you and inquire of you as to whether you'd heard from Mr. Dzankovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I can't confirm or deny that. Realistically speaking, it's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And, in fact, given the realities of the situation, what I suggest to you is that it's a highly likely thing to have happened, that Halilovic would have called you and made an inquiry in terms such as this that -- as to how Dzankovic was getting on with his inquiries. Is that a realistic proposition to put to you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by what I said in answer to your last question. What I see here is something else. The origin of this document, who taped this? Where did it come from? That's what I find very interesting as -- as a member of the security administration. In fact, more interesting than the conversation itself, because the conversation may as well have taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And just -- just on that topic, which may -- may prove to be a very important one. It certainly wasn't tape recorded by your service, to your knowledge, anyway, was it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise that it was. At that time, we didn't do that, as far as I remember. We didn't use that particular method.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But was it within your knowledge that operative measure, including tape recording of telephone conversations, was being applied by the State Security Services -- not by you but by the State Security Services to Mr. Halilovic. I suppose I should put that question in two parts: Were you aware of it at the time of these events? That's the first question. And secondly, if not, did you become aware that that was taking place at any subsequent time?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I took up my present position on or about the 17th of July. Prior to that date, I had not been aware of any operative measures being applied in relation to Mr. Sefer Halilovic while carrying out preparations for Trebevic I and Trebevic II operations. There was an enormous amount of information from the State Security Service, from the 1st Corps, some information from the 4th Corps. On several occasions - and I think we referred to this yesterday - there were overlaps. There was information overlap which obviously came about as a result of phone line tapping. I did ask what was going on, but I didn't know Mr. Halilovic was a high-ranking officer. I can't tie this down to a specific time or place, but if memory serves, an answer came from the State Security Service that they were indeed applying this measure as some form of operative control, that the Secret Services were doing this, their counter-intelligence. They had measures that were prescribed, and this was one of them. Again, operative control was something that was applied according to a set of rules, and the purpose was to monitor everything that was suspicious or that required checking and to verify whether these potential threats were still real or ongoing. Once something ceased to be of interest, the operative measures would be dropped. These operative measures were by no means to be misused in order to prejudice or hurt in any way the person that the measure was being applied on. If indeed it turned out that some indications persisted, then the measures would continue to be applied until such time as these indications ceased and until such time as there was no longer any need to apply these measures that I refer to as "operative control." Why did the State Security Service do this? I was asking myself the same question. For the most part, the answer was - and I can't be more specific about it - that this had already been introduced at an earlier stage based on information obtained by the State Security Service, information indicating that Mr. Sefer Halilovic had been a secret associate of the former JNA security service, and that the measure had been adopted following approval by the state president and following approval by the Minister of the Interior. This was a wartime situation, so they came up with a legal justification, saying that that service, too, was also under the jurisdiction of the army and that this was their platform for taking this measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. You --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With no ill intent towards Mr. Halilovic. That's what they said. I'm not sure if I've been successful in explaining this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, you have been. And I just wanted to clarify one short point about that. As to the basis on which the State Security took that action, you only know what you were told by them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I personally had no other information regarding that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, in -- in light of the witness's comments of not having seen in document in any form, I'm not going to seek to tender that one, so that that can be returned. I'd ask that the witness please be given the opportunity now to look at another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This document is Defence 65 ter number -- Your Honour, I'm happy for that to remain -- for the Prosecutors to retain a copy, even though I haven't sought to tender it. I don't seek to leave one with the Court in order to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I gave it an MFI number. I don't think it's proper to leave it with the Court when I'm not seeking to tender it. I don't know how to resolve that problem though, and I just indicate I don't seek to leave it there to leave an impression of any sort, if it's ... Anyway, the next document is -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: You've withdrawn the document, so you have withdrawn the MFI and we can use the next MFI, 234.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I will seek the use that MFI now in relation to another document, which is DD00.0130.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This document -- do you have that document in front of you that appears to be dated 24th of September, 1993 and to originate from Nermin Eminovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document before me. It's not very clear. But I think the date up in the heading is the 14th of September and not the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm sorry, it's -- I've got the English version. Just excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the -- the date in question is at the top left of the first page, and I wonder if that could be enlarged so that the witness could view an enlarged version of it. And meanwhile, Your Honour, a paper copy will be procured. It's the -- the top left of the page is what's needed, I'm sorry to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I'm going to try to get an expanded version of that so that you can view the -- the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, what's on the screen in front of me right now -- oh, yes, it does -- sorry, pardon me. It does have what's needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you able to see now -- in the -- in the section at the top left of the page, the date which at least is at sometime in the -- in September 1993. And when you look closely at that -- at the digits there, what's your view? Do you say that looks like a "14th of the 9th" or "the 24th of the 9th"?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the top left, it looks very much like "24," this figure here. But I think if we look at the incoming stamp, the number will be much easier to discern. If you look there, you will see that it was after all the 14th, because the incoming stamp says "15." There is no way it could have been received on the 15th if it had been sent on the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I said at the start that you were fully entitled to correct us as to dates, and I'm very grateful that you have. By looking at that -- at that document, are you able to make the comment that this -- you can comment that this document is -- was whatever date may appear, whether it's 24th or 14th, the fact is it was received by -- by your organisation on the 15th of September, which probably concludes the issue. Very well. Well, in relation to that document there, we are -- I'm sorry to say, we're jumping a little bit out of time now. And when I prepare -- I'm going to prepare list of these documents later for ease of handling. But this document probably occurred a little bit earlier. Again, this is a -- a document quite early in the -- in the investigation, and it appears from that point of view to repeat the comment about Vehbija Karic. Do you recall receiving this document?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, I won't go -- I won't go back through the document, but do you remember earlier on there was a document that we looked at which referred to another letter dated on the 14th of September? Do you remember that occurring?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really put the two together, but I can comment on this: This is in response to my first document, with that initiative I spoke about. I sent it out on the 12th based on verified information, and so on and so forth, and then those two tasks. It's about those two tasks that he should check whether it was true or not, and if true, that he should speak to the commander to recommend for the military police to get involved so that arrests can be made. This is his reply to that document. And I can see the reference at the top of the page, "your document dated the 12th of September." All these things that were underlined and the question marks, these are the marks that I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise my own marks. And what you can see here, these proposals and assignments written by hand, I wrote all of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And just to finally conclude this matter, you have made it possible in this document to trace back the letter to which it's responding because at the top you've referred -- at the top of the text, after the addresses, you've referred to a document "03/5-108" of 12 September 1993, and so if we have the number with that -- the document with that number on it, then we know we have the correct document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF JASAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document that I sent on the 12th to the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just interject for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: This is the very same document that we showed it as Prosecution MFI214. It's the same document that I -- in my examination-in-chief. I thought I'd indicate that so that -- it's the same document, Your Honour. And the date on ours is the 14th in the Bosnian version, and it's been translated somewhere as the 16th of September in the English, but I think we should obviously take the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, yes, I'm grateful for that indication, and -- yeah, I think -- just for continuity I may -- I may stick to the number that we are using, if that's okay. But I think it should be noted by my friend, as she's mentioned, that it's the same document or a copy of it. We're not quite sure about that, but it's likely to be the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we finish, could I just -- just raise one matter? MFI224 is a document that was tendered earlier on. That number -- without going back through the computer and bringing it all up again over five minutes, can I indicate that that document, MFI224 is indeed the order of the 12th and it indeed has the numbers referred to, 03/5-108.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just indicate now that I'm moving through a number of documents. I -- my estimate was wrong. I apologise for that. And I'm very grateful to the court staff for handling this volume of documents. I'm putting the e-court under some pressure but it has stood up well. I expect to be no more than an hour with this witness tomorrow, and really what remains is document work of the nature that has occurred today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, we will request both parties to submit a list containing the documents which they are going to tender through this witness by tomorrow, because since we have so many documents, it's very difficult to identify which document is used and which document is going to tender through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I hope one party should furnish that list to the other party, as well as to the Bench and the court deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If there's any problem with the numbers, please check it with our court deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Morrissey, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm just asked to clarify the timing of tomorrow, that you would like that done, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before -- before the afternoon sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Well, that -- that will mean our list is incomplete because I haven't -- I won't have finished cross-examination. But it's very predictable what I'm going to put tomorrow, and assuming that -- I think most of it ought to be uncontroversial. So yes, of course, we will comply with that. And also we will speak to the Prosecutors. It may be we can do it in a form, Your Honour, which will allows Your Honour to deal with any controversy over admission as well at the end of this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So, witness, you have to come back tomorrow, and I believe that you still remember my warnings to you, and we'll see you tomorrow afternoon. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 4th day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.
